note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: Moody's SPARED France (Oct 23): Aa3 affirmed, negative outlook — vs the widely expected A1 cut; wants a deficit-cutting 2027 budget, debt >120% of GDP in 2027; S&P reviews France Nov 27. OAT-Bund ~167bp (Oct 27) vs 170-177bp (15-yr high); France 10Y 5.14% (highest since July 2002); revenue-section vote moved to Nov 3 (was Oct 27); unions strike Nov 5. UK: Healey's first Budget Wednesday (CGT rise off the table, bank tax £2-5B, headroom £23.6B→~£15B). No US shutdown — CR through Dec 11.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: German Ifo Mon 90.2 beat (6th straight rise, highest since May 2023; expectations 91.6 best in 4.5+ yrs, current conditions 88.8 softer); UK CBI Oct -10 big beat (slowest retail fall since Apr 2025; sterling eased anyway pre-Budget). US Dallas Fed Oct 13.4 beat (vs 7.0 fcst, Sep 9.8) — new orders collapsed 30.7 to 9.3, production 15.8, prices paid 55.3; CFNAI Sep +0.07 beat (MA3 +0.03, just above trend). US Q3 GDP advance Thu (cons 3.0% SAAR, GDPNow 3.5%); EZ Q3 GDP Fri; German Q3 GDP Fri; Canada Aug GDP Fri. Last week: US claims 194K (near 57-yr lows), flash comp 57.6 inline; EZ comp 51.9 miss (France 48.4 contraction); UK comp 53.1 beat; AU comp 47.7 miss (first contraction in 5 months). Tue Oct 27 (NY close): durable goods +1.8% beat, confidence 91.7 big beat (biggest since May 2025), new home sales 676K beat — dollar firmed into the close on the data + pre-FOMC caution.
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: US Sep PCE Thu (headline +0.5% m/m exp — largest since March; core +0.3% m/m); AU Q3 CPI Tue 7:30pm CT (trimmed +1.0% q/q consensus; Hauser 'materially worse'); EZ flash CPI Fri; German flash CPI Fri; Tokyo CPI Thu. US CPI 3.7%, import prices +8.1% y/y; Brent ~$115.15 Tuesday Asia (from $116.72 Friday close) — energy premium easing, not gone. Overnight: UK BRC shop prices beat 2.1% (fastest since Feb 2024); Japan services PPI inline at 3.7%.
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: Triple-decision Wednesday: RBNZ 8pm CT Tue (hike ~85-89% to 3.00%), BoC 8:45am CT (hike ~75-80%; TD dissents), FOMC 1pm CT (hold ~89-93% LSEG 89.5%; Dec hike ~73-82%; blackout). ECB Thu 8:15am CT (hold ~93-97%; presser on OATs/TPI). BoJ Fri (hold; Dec ~83-88%; Outlook Report). RBA Nov 2-3 (~50/50; Q3 CPI Wed the pivot).
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). When nearly everyone has made the same bet, it can unwind fast: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: New CFTC (Oct 20, released Oct 23): euro net short largest since Mar-2020 (contrarian +1 — squeeze side up); hedge funds cut yen shorts, added AUD longs, more bearish CAD (net short largest since early Aug — squeeze fuel into BoC); more bullish GBP. Dollar longs <$40B (down from $44.5B). No crowded-long unwind risk — the pain trade is the euro-short squeeze.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Haven bid fading: dollar firmer in London morning (DXY ~102.04-102.09; EUR/USD 1.1154, USD/JPY 157.73) as steadier equities stall last week's AI-rout haven play (Reuters, Oct 27); ING: markets reconnecting with the hawkish-Fed + high-energy backdrop. Mediation moving on two tracks, nothing agreed: Qatari mediators in Tehran Sunday (US-coordinated); Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials in Tehran Monday. Houthis claimed Monday strikes on East-West pipeline pumping stations and Riyadh airport; Saudi reported intercepts, no damage confirmation. Finance Minister Katayama (Tue): Tokyo stands ready to act decisively in FX. VIX ~18.4 (Shunya pre-market). NY close: DXY ~102.3 (+0.26%, 1.5-week high), EUR/USD 1.1136 (5th down day), USD/JPY 157.80.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Brent $115.15 Tuesday Asia (-0.57%); settled $115.81 Monday (-0.8%) after Friday's $116.72 close (+6.2% wk — highest close since April); WTI $100.80 (-0.94%). Qatari mediators in Tehran Sunday (US-coordinated) and Saudi/Turkish/Pakistani officials in Tehran Monday eased the immediate escalation bid, but Houthi claims on the East-West pipeline pumping stations and Riyadh airport (no Riyadh confirmation) kept the premium in. Energy-exporter tailwind (CAD, AUD); energy-importer tax (EUR, JPY). Gold ~$4,020 — back above $4,000 after Monday's dip.
tot.title: Terms of trade
